item.title: Following big Democratic wins, these swing voters are looking for results
item.description: For the swing voters NPR is regularly checking in with as part of its Swing Shift series, the election results brought mixed emotions, as does the pending Democratic control of Congress.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to a large exchange of prisoners of war, officials say
item.description: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war. U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi led to this decision, marking the biggest humanitarian release since the war began in 2022.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: House effectively ends Hegseth impeachment. And, 3 men accused of plotting U.K. attacks
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has been spared from the House's impeachment effort, at least for now. And, federal prosecutors arrested three men accused of being Iran-backed operatives.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Iran-backed trio accused of plotting attacks on U.K. base hosting U.S. jets
item.description: Iran-backed operatives have been charged over nearly 20 attacks, including a plot on a U.K. base housing U.S. troops. Separately, a U.S. soldier is held in the U.K. on Russia spying claims.

item.title: Both sides now? Critics slam DOJ moves to dismiss convictions of Trump allies
item.description: The DOJ moved to dismiss criminal convictions of former Trump adviser Steve Bannon and of the Oath Keepers, in what it calls "the interests of justice." Critics are crying foul.

item.title: Oil giant ExxonMobil left Venezuela years ago. Now it's considering a return

item.title: U.S. officials look to Europe to learn how to make prison better
item.description: American prison officials are looking to European nations like Germany and Norway for a roadmap on how to design a prison that emphasizes rehabilitation and a successful return to life on the outside.
